Hi Ben / Marissa / Laura,

Thanks for taking this — we are compiling a short vendor residency & deletion checklist for our procurement and security teams. Can you confirm the following for Redwood’s hosted inference API (and note any differences for Dedicated/Private deployments):

1) Where are inference requests executed (primary regions and fallback regions)? Do any parts of the request ever leave those regions (e.g., metadata routing, telemetry, support hops)?
2) Which subprocessors are involved in execution, caching, logging, and KMS (please list vendor + rough region footprint)?
3) What are your default retention windows for request payloads, KV cache, request logs, and backups?
4) If we submit a deletion request for a customer account, what is the end-to-end timeline (logical deletion, physical deletion from live stores, backup expiration)? How do you provide evidence to us?

I've attached our checklist (Solstice_Residency_Checklist.pdf) — we mostly need concise answers so procurement can move forward. If it helps, happy to do a quick 30-min call next week.

Hi Celia — answering the technical bullets below. I kept the hosted vs dedicated/private differences explicit.

1) Execution regions and routing
- Hosted API (default): requests are routed to the lowest-latency pool subject to tenant routing policy. Primary execution points today include: AWS us-west-2 (Oregon), AWS us-east-1 (N. Virginia), GCP europe-west4 (Netherlands), Azure west-europe (Netherlands), and GCP asia-southeast1 (Singapore).
- Dedicated: customer-reserved pools are pinned to the region(s) in the contract; we will not route traffic outside pinned regions unless you opt into cross-region burst.
- Private/on-prem: customer fully controls where inference executes.
- Cross-border notes: metadata for routing (region selection, health checks) may be processed by Redwood control-plane services in either the US or EU depending on account tenancy. Payloads are not copied to control-plane logs by default; telemetry is aggregated with identifiers where necessary.

2) Subprocessors (execution, caching, logging, KMS) — vendor + typical footprint
- Compute / execution: AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1), GCP (europe-west4, asia-southeast1), Azure (west-europe).
- Object storage / backups: S3 (AWS) and GCS (GCP) depending on region; buckets are region-scoped where possible.
- CDN / ingress: CloudFront and Cloudflare for edge networking and DDoS protection.
- KV cache / ephemeral caches: Redis clusters hosted on the same cloud region as execution; caches are ephemeral and TTL-controlled by workload.
- Logging & observability: Logs are ingested to a regional observability tier and retained per your org default (see next section). Subprocessors: Datadog (US/EU), internal ELK clusters.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault). When using customer-managed keys, key material never leaves the vendor KMS region.

3) Default retention windows (hosted API defaults; Dedicated/Private can be configured)
- Inference request payloads (transient): not persisted to long-term stores by default; persisted only to fulfill the request and to short-lived caches (seconds to minutes).
- KV cache: default TTL 24 hours, configurable down to minutes or disabled.
- Request logs (for debugging/traceability): 30 days default; can be shortened to 0 days for stricter retention plans on enterprise tiers.
- Backups / snapshots: weekly snapshots retained 45 days by default for disaster recovery; snapshot locations respect region pinning where possible. For EU-only accounts we offer EU-only backup placement.

4) Deletion workflow and timelines (hosted API)
- Logical delete (account or dataset mark-for-delete): completed within minutes of the request and prevents new processing.
- Live-store purge (active datasets, caches): typically completed within 24 hours; caches are invalidated immediately.
- Backup & snapshot expiration: backups are subject to backup retention windows and are removed at the next scheduled rotation; practical window 30–60 days depending on snapshot timing.
- Audit evidence: each deletion generates an audit record with timestamp, actor, and job id. For hosted customers we can export time-stamped evidence (CSV) and provide a signed attestation upon request. Dedicated customers can obtain more granular deletion tickets and proof-of-wipe on request.

Other operational notes:
- Support escalations: for expedited removal from backups we provide a defined emergency wipe workflow (requires contract amendment / higher-tier support).
- Export controls: if data needs to be constrained to EU-only processing we recommend Dedicated or Private to avoid transient control-plane hops; hosted accounts can be configured to prefer EU-only nodes but not guaranteed without region pinning.

Hi Celia / team — answering the legal + procurement items and next steps.

- Snapshot replication: by default snapshots are region-scoped. We do not replicate backups cross-region for hosted accounts unless configured for cross-region DR. If you require cross-region replication for resiliency, we configure explicit consent and document the target regions.

- Deletion evidence: yes — we can provide an automated export of deletion audit entries (CSV) with timestamp, Redwood job id, actor, and target account id. For hosted customers this is provided via a support ticket; for Dedicated we can automate exports into a secure bucket on a cadence.

- Emergency wipe SLA: standard emergency wipe is 72 hours from ticket acceptance; expedited wipes (24 hours or less) are available under an elevated support SLA and require a one-time operational fee and contractual amendment. We will include the SLA options in the statement of work.

- SCCs / DPA: Redwood’s DPA includes the EU SCCs as an option; we can provision a DPA with SCCs attached and provide a redline-ready Word doc. I’ve attached a doc with the clause references (SCC_clauses_doc.docx) and a link to our SOC 2 Type II summary in the evidence pack.

Next steps:
1) We’ll circulate the one-page tech summary + annotated topology (Marissa).
2) Procurement / legal can send redlines to me and we’ll aim to return a DPA draft within 3 business days.
3) If you choose Dedicated/EU-only, we’ll provide a formal quote and configuration worksheet for region pinning and backup placement.

If helpful, I can join your call on Tuesday to walk through the legal items.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
